Decision of Judgment All the accused persons namely  Sanjay, Raju, Sunita and  Bhawana are acquitted of the  charges framed against them.
BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE 1.

On 04.06.2020, a PCR call (having DD no.41A) was assigned to Sub Inspector Subendu Sharma at Police Station Sarojini Nagar, by which an information was received that a lady namely Anjali has committed suicide at H.No.16, Opposite Pilanji Park, Kalabadi Mandir, Palika Gram, Sarojini Nagar.
On this information, SI Subendu Sharma along with Ct. Vikram reached at the spot, where they found that lot of people were present outside the aforesaid house.
One girl namely Bhawana was also found outside the house.
On inquiry from the public persons, one person informed that one lady namely Anjali had committed suicide in the house and she has been taken to Safdarjung Hospital by her family members.
The girl Bhawana who was present there, also informed that her bhabhi i.e. Anjali had committed suicide.
Thereafter, SI Subendu Sharma called the Crime Team at the spot and after leaving Ct. Vikram there, he went to Safdarjung Hospital.
On reaching Safdarjung Hospital, he found Anjali in emergency ward on ventilator, she was not in a condition to give her statement.
He further collected the MLC of Anjali and reached back to the spot, where Crime Team was inspecting the place and were taking the photographs.
As seven years of marriage of Anjali were not completed, therefore the PS Sarojini Nagar concerned SDM of the area was informed about the incident.
On 05.06.2020, Anjali expired and SI Subendu Sharma got recorded the statements of Sushil, Mithilesh and Abhilash recorded by the concerned SDM.
Thereafter, information was sent to SHO concerned and on his directions, present FIR under Section 498A, 304B was registered in Police Station Sarojini Nagar.
2. On the aforesaid allegations, the investigation in the present matter was carried out and after completion of the investigation, charge-sheet was filed in the court.
The cognizance of the offence was taken.
Accused persons were summoned.
On 22.10.2020, after compliance of Section 207 of Criminal Procedure Code, the Ld. Magistrate committed the present case file to the Court of Sessions.
3. On 21.04.2022, charges were framed against the accused persons for the offences punishable under section 498A, 304B read with section 34 of Indian Penal Code.
Charges were read over to the accused persons, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
4. To prove its case, prosecution has examined 06 witnesses in all.

5. On 11.04.2023, accused persons admitted some of the prosecution witnesses vide their statement being recorded under section 294 CrPC.

In view of the admission, prosecution witnesses i.e. Sumit,
Abhishek, Manish, Ct. Mahesh, Dr. Alif Muzaffar, Sh. Vipul Sandwar, the then Ld. MM, SI Ajay, Ct.
Vikas, Ct. Mahesh, W/Ct. Reena, HC Virender and Ct. Balwant, were dropped from the list of witnesses.
6. After examination of the prosecution witnesses, the prosecution evidence was closed.
On 06.12.2023, statements of accused persons namely Sanjay, Raju, Sunita and Bhawana were recorded under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
In their statements, the accused persons have denied the allegations and submitted that they have been falsely implicated in the present case.
The accused persons did not lead any evidence in their defence and the matter was put for final arguments.
ARGUMENTS 7.
It is submitted by the Ld.
Counsel
for accused persons
that the testimony on record of the prosecution witnesses do not support the case of the prosecution, as PW-1/Abhilash and PW- 2/Mithilesh have resiled from their statements recorded u/s 161 CrPC.
Thus, accused persons are entitled for acquittal.

Ld. Additional Public Prosecutor strongly opposed the acquittal of the accused persons.

3 LAW ON THE SUBJECT 10.
It is relevant here to note the provision of Section 498A, 304B of Indian Penal Code and Section 113B of Indian Evidence Act.

For the purpose of reference, they are reproduced as under:
498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.-

Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

Explanation.- For the purpose of this section, ''cruelty'' means- (a) any willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.]

304B. Dowry death.- (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for,
or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called ''dowry death'', and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
Explanation.- For the purpose of this sub-section, ''dowry'' shall have PS Sarojini Nagar the same meaning as in section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
(2) Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life.]
113B. Presumption as to dowry death.

-- When the question is whether a person has committed the dowry death of a woman and it is shown that soon before her death such woman had been subjected by such person to cruelty or harassment for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, the court shall presume that such person had caused the dowry death.
Explanation.
For the purposes of this section, dowry death shall have the same meaning as in section 304B of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).
11. The ingredients of Section 304B and 498A of IPC were discussed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Baijnath Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh (2017) 1 SCC 101.

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraphs are reproduced as under:
"25.

Whereas in the offence of dowry death defined by Section 304B of the Code, the ingredients thereof are:

4 (i) death of the woman concerned is by any burns or bodily injury or by any cause other than in normal circumstance, and (ii) is within seven years of her marriage, and (iii) that soon before her death, she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of the husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry.
The offence under Section 498A of the Code is attracted qua the husband or his relative if she is subjected to cruelty.

The explanation to this Section exposits "cruelty" as:
(I) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical), or (ii) harassment of the woman, where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
PS Sarojini Nagar 26.

Patently thus, cruelty or harassment of the lady by her husband or his relative for or in connection with any demand for any property or valuable security as a demand for dowry or in connection therewith is the common constituent of both the offences.
27. The expression "dowry" is ordained to have the same meaning as in Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
The expression "cruelty", as explained, contains in its expanse, apart from the conduct of the tormentor, the consequences precipitated thereby qua the lady subjected thereto.
Be that as it may, cruelty or harassment by the husband or any relative of his for or in connection with any demand of dowry to reiterate is the gravamen of the two offences."
12. In the case of Baijnath Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh (supra), in paragraphs 29 and 30, the presumption under Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act was also discussed.

For the purpose of reference, Section 29 and 30 are reproduced as under:
29.
Noticeably, this presumption as well is founded on the proof of cruelty or harassment of the woman dead for or in connection with any demand for dowry by the person charged with the offence.

The presumption as to dowry death thus would get activated only upon the proof of fact that the deceased lady had been subjected to cruelty or harassment for or in connection with any demand for dowry by the accused and that too in the reasonable contiguity of death.

Such a proof is thus the legislatively mandated prerequisite to invoke the otherwise statutorily ordained State vs Sanjay And Ors on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57610359/
5 presumption of commission of offence of dowry death by the person charged therewith.

30. A conjoint reading of these three provisions, thus predicate the burden of the prosecution to unassailably substantiate the ingredients of the two offences by direct and convincing evidence so as to avail the presumption engrafted in Section 113B of the Act against the accused.

Proof of cruelty or harassment by the husband or his relative or the person charged is thus the sine qua non to inspirit the statutory presumption, to draw the person charged within the coils thereof.

If the prosecution fails to demonstrate by cogent, coherent and persuasive evidence to prove such fact,
the person accused of either of the above referred offences cannot be held guilty by taking refuge only of the presumption to cover up the shortfall in proof."

sentences.text: In the latter pronouncement, this Court propounded that one of the essential ingredients of dowry death under Section 304 B of the Code is that the accused must have subjected the woman to cruelty in connection with demand for dowry soon before her death and that this ingredient has to be proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt and only then the Court will presume that the accused has committed the offence of dowry death under Section 113B of the Act.

It referred to with approval, the earlier decision of this Court in K. Prema S. Rao v. Yadla Srinivasa Rao, (2003) 1 SCC 217 : 2003 SCC (Cri) 271 to the effect that to attract the provision of Section 304B of the Code, one of the main ingredients of the offence which is required to be established is that "soon before her death" she was subjected to cruelty and harassment "in connection with the demand for dowry".

In light of the legal position stated above, the matter in hand is now to be examined i.e. it has to be seen by this court, as to whether the case falls in the category where the presumption can be raised against the accused, relieving the prosecution from proving its case and putting the onus on the accused persons.

6 15.
The marriage of the deceased Anjali was solemnized on 17.01.2017.

On 05.06.2020, FIR was registered on the complaint of complainant Sushil Kumar i.e. the father of the deceased PS Sarojini Nagar Anjali, against accused persons namely Sanjay, Raju, Sunita and Bhawana.
PW-1 Abhilash (brother of the deceased) deposed about the date of marriage of his deceased sister with accused Sanjay as being 17.01.2017.

This witness also confirmed the fact about the residence of the deceased with accused Sanjay was at H.No. 16, Sarojini Nagar, NDMC Quarter, New Delhi, and that she was residing with her father-in-law, mother-in-law, sisters-in- law namely Sunita and Bhawana and brother-in-law Yuvraj.
This witness deposed that, when he returned home in the evening of 04.06.2020, he received a call from a neighbour that his sister Anjali had committed suicide by hanging herself.
On receiving this calls, he immediately left for the house of Anjali and found that public persons were gathered outside the house.
Although her sister Anjali was taken to Safdarjung Hospital by her in-laws.
In the testimony of this witness, he specifically deposed that he is unaware of the reason of suicide of his sister.
This witness was cross-examined by the State, however in the cross-examination also, the witness denied the contents of his statement recorded u/s 161 CrPC.
16. PW-2 Smt. Mithilesh (mother of deceased Anjali), she testified that she received a telephonic call from neighbours of her daughter Anjali, informing about her death.
On this, she went to the house of her daughter and from there to the hospital.
This witness also deposed that she do not have any knowledge with respect to the reason of the suicide.

This witness was also cross- examined by the State in depth, however this witness denied the fact that at the time of marriage, accused Raju had asked for PS Sarojini Nagar cash, in addition to dowry articles, as the cash of Rs.50,000/- was only given, therefore, the accused persons started harassing deceased Anjali.
Thus, this witness was put to cross-examination by the State, but nothing came which can support the version of prosecution.
The opportunity to cross-examine this witness was given to the defence counsel, however Ld.
defence counsel did not ask any question thereto.

17. PW-3 Manoj, he is independent witness, who deposed that on the date of the incident i.e.
04.06.2020 at about 07:15 PM, he was walking in colony.
At about 08:00 PM, he heard huge noise from 1st floor of Flat No. 16.

On hearing the same, he went to the plot, where he saw lot of people being gathered outside the house, as the gate of floor was locked from inside; with the help of some persons, gate was opened and it was seen that one lady namely Anjali was hanging from the ceiling fan.
This witness deposed that husband of lady Anjali was standing outside the room and he also entered with them.
The opportunity to cross- examine this witness was given to the Ld. Defence Counsel, but he chose not to cross-examine this witness.
18. PW-4 is the Executive Magistrate, who, on the instructions of SDM Vasant Vihar, recorded the statement of father, mother and brother of the deceased.
In the testimony, he exhibited his letter of authority.
This witness was cross-examined, in which he deposed that he do not have any personal knowledge about the incident.

On inquiry from the public persons, one person informed that a lady namely Anjali committed suicide in the house and she had been taken to Safdarjung Hospital by her family members.
The girl Bhawana who was present there, also informed that her bhabhi i.e. Anjali had committed suicide.
Thereafter, IO/SI Subendu Sharma called the Crime Team at the spot and after leaving Ct. Vikram, he went to Safdarjung Hospital.
On reaching Safdarjung Hospital, he found Anjali in emergency ward on ventilator, as she was not in a condition to give her statement.
He further collected the MLC of Anjali and reached back to the spot, where the Crime Team was inspecting the place and were taking the photographs.

This witness was cross-examined by the Ld.
Defence Counsel.
20. PW-6 is Inspector Narender, the further investigation in the present matter was marked to him on the directions of the concerned SHO.
He alongwith Investigating Officer/ SI Subendu Sharma and with other staff, went to mortuary of Safdarjung Hospital and after necessary formalities, got conducted postmortem of deceased Anjali.
After the postmortem PS Sarojini Nagar proceeding, the body of Anjali was handed over to the complainant namely Sushil.
This witness seized the viscera and nail clipping with seizure memo Ex.PW5/Q.
This witness also recorded statements of public witnesses namely Abhishek, Manoj, Manish and Sumit.
This witness arrested accused Sanjay (husband of deceased) and later on, got him produced before the Ld. Magistrate.

After some days,
he recorded statement of father of deceased namely Sushil Kumar and on his directions, statement u/s 164 CrPC was recorded of Sushil Kumar.
During the course of investigation, this witness also recorded statement of mother of deceased namely Smt. Mithilesh and brother of deceased namely Abhilash.

During the investigation, co-accused persons namely Raju, Sunita and Bhawana were also arrested and their disclosures statements were recorded, which were exhibited as Ex.PW5/L,
Ex.PW5/M and Ex.PW5/N.
After further necessary investigation, charge-sheet was filed in the court.
This witness was cross-examined by the Ld. Defence Counsel.
In the cross-examination, this witness supported his version given at the time of recording of his examination-in-chief.
21. I have perused the case file thoroughly.
CONCLUSION 22.

In the aforesaid evidence led by the prosecution, none of the witnesses stated about the cruelty or harassment to the deceased by the accused persons on account of demand of dowry soon before the death or otherwise.
In fact, harassment has not been narrated by anyone.

Also, in the cross-examination by the PS Sarojini Nagar State, PW-2 Smt. Mithilesh, who is the mother of the deceased, she categorically denied that at the time of marriage, accused Raju demanded cash and dowry articles, and that as only Rs.50,000/- cash was given therefore, her daughter was put to harassment and cruelty.
The aforesaid evidence led by the prosecution does not fulfil the prerequisite to invoke presumption under section 304B IPC or section 113B of Indian Evidence Act.
Even the ingredients of section 498A IPC are not made out, as there is no evidence on record proving cruelty or harassment of the deceased.

State vs Sanjay And Ors on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57610359/
8 23.
Thus, this court is of the view that prerequisite for section 498A IPC and to raise presumption under section 304B IPC and Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act, are not being made out.
The death simplicitor being unnatural in the matrimonial home within 07 years of marriage, cannot be sufficient reason to convict accused persons for the offence mentioned above.

24. In view of the above observations, accused persons namely Sanjay, Raju, Sunita and Bhawana have been acquitted of all the charges punishable under section 498A, 304B read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code.
